angle.text: Subscription tracker: dates, decisions and proof

copy.text: Subscription tracker: dates, decisions and proof

scenes.why: The hook is the guide's own title: the question it answers, as a person would put it.

copy.text: Verify the billing channel and next charge in the actual account.
Read the cancellation terms and record any cutoff separately.
Enter the full upcoming charge even if you also calculate a monthly equivalent.
Choose keep, review or cancel, and assign an action date before the cutoff.

eyebrow.text: Set up the next action, not just the row

scenes.why: The guide's own checklist, the first sentence of each item, ticked in as it is read.

caption.text: Add what you have across the seven areas: accounts, income, bills, subscriptions, transactions, debt, and savings.

scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "Records" (What's actually true right now, area by area: accounts, income, bills, subscriptions, transactions, debt.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "Add what you have across the seven areas: accounts, income, bills, subscriptions"; focus on "Accounts".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: YouTube Short, 1080×1920, 18–45s, hook by 1.2s, sound on
reasoning.because: Search-adjacent audience that will watch a slightly longer explanation if it starts strong. Loops by default.

reasoning.decision: Personal Finance Companion: $49 (list $99), motif "index", calm personality, cool accent #0d3b2e
reasoning.because: From its definition and Shop listing. 4 real screens to show.
Teaches from the guide first; Personal Finance Companion is the product the guide hands over to. 1 lists and timelines, 3 questions to draw from.

reasoning.decision: Before launch: helpful and relatable only
reasoning.because: Nobody knows Draftpace yet, so films show how it helps with real moments. Who it is not for, questions before buying, what you get and the price wait until there are users to sell to.

reasoning.decision: You have more than one account, bill, or income source and want them tracked in one real place, not five apps. / You want a next step handed to you, not a dashboard you have to interpret yourself every time.
reasoning.because: The listing's own audience lines; the director writes for them.

reasoning.decision: Allowed real lines up to 4 words longer
reasoning.because: Every structure Personal Finance Companion's copy supports at YouTube Short's normal line length is already used by its other films; a longer real line beats telling the same story twice.

reasoning.decision: The checklist: The guide's checklist on one screen, item by item, then the product that holds it.
reasoning.because: Best fit for a awareness film on YouTube Short (platform fit 2, goal fit 3, already used for this product ×3, already used on YouTube Short ×10). Other candidates: The question people ask (-44.9).
A checklist from the guide, "Set up the next action, not just the row": 4 of its 7 items.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "index"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "index": an index of tabs, so scenes slide in like the next tab.
Camera "dolly": constant forward movement for a high-energy feed.
Grounds ink → light → light → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Its shape was 0.74 similar to guide-fall-home-maintenance-checklist--youtube-short; a different film, not the same one re-coloured.
Its shape was 0.82 similar to guide-where-is-my-water-shutoff--youtube-short; a different film, not the same one re-coloured.

Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on YouTube Short (0.26s a word), inside 18–45s.
